clue.text: Cat — middle of well — in awkward situation

indicators.note: the middle letters go inside the word for a tight spot

parts.note: to be in a fix is to be in an awkward situation

indicators.note: the centre pair of letters of the word well is taken

explanation.surface: A cat has got itself stuck down a well and is in a tricky spot.
explanation.walkthrough: The dashes make 'middle of well' look like an aside, but it supplies letters; Felix is a famous cartoon cat and a common name for pet cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Felix the Cat is a classic cartoon feline, and the name is a byword for a pet cat.

clue.text: Pirate captain-has to secure a firearm

parts.note: Captain Flint is the pirate in Stevenson's Treasure Island
to secure a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: A pirate captain makes sure he keeps hold of his gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Flint is the dead pirate whose treasure drives Treasure Island (Long John Silver's parrot is named after him). 'has to' and 'a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An old type of gun fired by a spark struck from flint against steel.

clue.text: Near beer to be had here?

definitions.meaning: nearby, in the neighbourhood
a pub close to home is where you go for a pint

explanation.definitionFit: Local means in the vicinity, and in Britain a local is one's neighbourhood pub, where beer is served.

clue.text: To play this you must knock on wood

definitions.text: To play this you must knock on wood

parts.words: To play this you must knock on wood
parts.note: reads like the superstition of touching wood for luck, but describes striking wooden bars with hammers to make music

explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument played by striking tuned wooden bars with small mallets.

clue.text: Trophy held in disrespect for the glare of publicity

indicators.note: one word is gripped inside the other, so the cup sits within the insult

parts.note: a slight is an act of disrespect
a pot is slang for a cup won as a trophy

explanation.surface: A celebrity's award is snubbed in full view of the press.
explanation.walkthrough: Pot as a trophy is sporting slang for a cup won in competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the spotlight is to be the focus of public attention, as if lit on stage.

clue.text: Thrift makes' us become only mildly enraged, say?

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken and the spelling heard differently

parts.note: to see red is to be furious, so to see pink is to be only a little annoyed

explanation.surface: Frugal living, the clue suggests, only irritates us a little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thrift' looks like frugality; it is the seaside plant, also called sea pink. 'say' signals that SEE PINK, a jokey milder version of 'see red', sounds the same as SEA PINK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea pink is another name for the coastal plant thrift, which has pink flower heads.

clue.text: What a short dance!

parts.note: an exclamation at a brief dance, also read as a dance made of a single pace

explanation.definitionFit: An early twentieth-century ballroom dance in quick time, its name suggesting just a single pace.

clue.text: Hard-hearted king whose widow was merry

indicators.note: having something at the heart means it is placed in the middle

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic monarch
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A stern monarch's widow seems rather cheerful after his death.
explanation.walkthrough: '-hearted' places H inside LEAR. Franz Lehár composed the operetta The Merry Widow, so the definition describes him by his best-known work.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hungarian composer wrote The Merry Widow, so his 'widow' was famously merry.

clue.text: Imitate Horatio's "sheeted dead" to his embarrassment? Nonsense!

parts.note: in Hamlet Horatio says the sheeted dead did squeak and gibber in the Roman streets

indicators.note: embarrassment throws the little word his into disorder

explanation.surface: Copying a line about ghosts from Hamlet would make one blush for talking rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio's speech in Hamlet (I.i) says 'the sheeted dead / Did squeak and gibber'. 'embarrassment' scrambles HIS into ISH; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish is meaningless talk, just like nonsense.

clue.text: Your old yours truly, Herb

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me, the speaker

explanation.surface: A letter signed off in old-fashioned style to someone called Herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' poses as a man's name signing a letter; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A culinary herb with small aromatic leaves.

clue.text: Blame for writing in copperplate perhaps

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters might be arranged another way

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, followed by plate

explanation.surface: A scribe is faulted for his ornate handwriting.
explanation.walkthrough: Copperplate gives CU (copper's symbol) plus PLATE; with IN that makes INCUPLATE, which 'perhaps' rearranges by swapping two letters. 'for writing' is linking padding.
explanation.definitionFit: To inculpate someone is to accuse or incriminate them.

clue.text: Spare-time occupation riding this horse?

definitions.meaning: a pastime or leisure pursuit
a ...-horse is a toy horse, and a favourite topic someone rides

explanation.definitionFit: A hobby is a pastime, and a hobby-horse is the toy horse on a stick.

clue.text: "Here --s bloom as they are told" (Brooke)

parts.note: a gap to fill from Rupert Brooke's poem about Grantchester, contrasting orderly German flowers

explanation.definitionFit: In Brooke's 'The Old Vicarage, Grantchester', the regimented spring flowers of Berlin bloom on command.

clue.text: Step in with tender and icebreaker

indicators.note: a breaker smashes things, so the preceding letters are broken up

explanation.surface: Someone intervenes, armed with a supply boat and an icebreaking ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'icebreaker' looks like one ship, but 'ice' is fodder and 'breaker' the anagram signal on TENDER plus ICE. A tender is a supply boat, making a nautical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to intervene on someone's behalf.

clue.text: Prospect — or aspect if one's bold, say?

definitions.meaning: the view of what lies ahead
a bold person's appearance is an out-and-out, forward look

explanation.definitionFit: An outlook is a view of the future, and read as out-look it is an outgoing, bold appearance.

clue.text: For markings in court distraught master holds student in

indicators.note: the jumbled letters enclose the next pieces
being distraught means the word master is thrown into confusion

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter, standing for a student
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upset schoolmaster keeps a pupil indoors, apparently near a tennis court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' turns MASTER into TRAMES (the letters the inserted pieces split as TRAM...ES); L is the learner's plate. 'For' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramlines are the pair of parallel side lines on a tennis or badminton court.

clue.text: Reward that may be paid as a matter of policy

definitions.meaning: a bonus or prize

definitions.text: that may be paid as a matter of policy
definitions.meaning: the regular sum handed over for an insurance policy

explanation.definitionFit: A premium is both a bonus or prize and the payment that keeps an insurance policy running.

clue.text: Law-making as the function of players

definitions.meaning: the passing of a statute
acting out a part, as actors do

explanation.definitionFit: Enactment is both the making of a law and the acting out of a role on stage.

clue.text: Vegetable, well-rounded, the pea

parts.note: a marrow is a large vegetable of the squash family
plump, so fat

explanation.surface: A list of plump produce in the vegetable garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vegetable' looks like the definition but supplies MARROW; the definition is at the other end.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrowfat is a variety of large, wrinkled pea, used for mushy peas.

clue.text: Dirty work bringing little honour to the railway

parts.note: in card games the knave or jack is the lowest of the honour cards
RY is a standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Grubby labour on the railway earns few accolades.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the honours are ace, king, queen, jack and ten; the knave (jack) is a small one. 'bringing ... to' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Knavery is dishonest, roguish behaviour.

clue.text: You will, it's said, surpass record for winter fuel

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece goes above, so it surpasses the next
it's said marks the words as heard rather than written

parts.note: you will contracts to you'll
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: You'll beat the record for heating your home this winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surpass' places YULE above LOG in a down answer; a log is a record, as in a ship's log.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yule log is a large log traditionally burned on the hearth at Christmas.

clue.text: What to do if she's frigid?

definitions.text: What to do if she's frigid?

parts.words: What to do if she's frigid?
parts.note: advice for warming a cold woman, also hiding a moorland shrub

explanation.definitionFit: Heather is the low flowering shrub of moors, and split it is advice to warm a woman.

clue.text: Refuge in the middle of the garden retreat

indicators.note: the centre letter of the little word the is chosen

parts.note: an arbour is a shady bower in a garden

explanation.surface: Someone takes shelter in the middle of the garden's shady nook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle of' picks H from tHe; it reads like a location but is the selection signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A harbour is a place of shelter, for ships or anyone in need.

clue.text: Call me with our revised description of compound structure

indicators.note: revised means these words are rewritten into a new order

explanation.surface: Ring the speaker to go over the account of a chemical's make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces of fodder; it is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Molecular describes things at the level of molecules, the structure of chemical compounds.

clue.text: A wee drop in the bar

definitions.meaning: a tiny liquid measure, one sixtieth of a fluid drachm
a musical note found in a bar of music

explanation.definitionFit: A minim is both an apothecaries' fluid measure of about one drop and a half note in music.

clue.text: Status of a saint in the Church

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the abbreviation for the Church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Asking what rank a saint holds in the Church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE (Church of England) is a standard crossword abbreviation; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Caste is a hereditary social class, hence one's standing in society.

clue.text: Trunk found in the forest or somewhere else

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tree trunk turns up in the woods or some other place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree in the forest, but it is the body's trunk; 'else' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human trunk, the body without head or limbs.

clue.text: Old official with rough-sounding spouse

definitions.meaning: a medieval local magistrate or manor steward
the female partner of the ruff, a bird whose name sounds like rough

explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a medieval local administrator, and the reeve is the female of the ruff, a wading bird.

clue.text: Dressing up? Clementine's shoes are the limit!

definitions.meaning: dressed to the ... means dressed very smartly
in the song Oh My Darling, Clementine, her shoes were number nine, the largest size

explanation.definitionFit: To be dressed to the nines is to wear one's finest; Clementine's shoes were number nine.

clue.text: Does such a book define "deciduous"?

parts.note: a binder with removable pages, read as describing trees that shed foliage

explanation.definitionFit: A binder whose pages can be removed, and deciduous trees literally let their foliage go.

clue.text: Mercury, for example, is a runner

definitions.meaning: Mercury was the ... of the Roman gods
one who carries messages on foot

explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was the gods' herald, and a runner carries messages.

clue.text: Negotiate free entertainment

definitions.meaning: to bargain with them
something paid for by another as a gift

explanation.definitionFit: To treat with is to negotiate, and a treat is entertainment someone else pays for.
